jobs.title: Senior Data Scientist — Data Cloud Acceleration
jobs.jd:
WHO WE ARE 

Zeta Global (NYSE: ZETA) is the AI-Powered Marketing Cloud that leverages advanced artificial intelligence (AI) and trillions of consumer signals to make it easier for marketers to acquire, grow, and retain customers more efficiently. Through the Zeta Marketing Platform (ZMP), our vision is to make sophisticated marketing simple by unifying identity, intelligence, and omnichannel activation into a single platform – powered by one of the industry’s largest proprietary databases and AI. Our enterprise customers across multiple verticals are empowered to personalize experiences with consumers at an individual level across every channel, delivering better results for marketing programs. Zeta was founded in 2007 by David A. Steinberg and John Sculley and is headquartered in New York City with offices around the world. To learn more, go to www.zetaglobal.com.

About the team 

The Data Cloud Acceleration team identifies gaps and opportunities across clients and business units, then moves quickly to deliver practical new capabilities. We often develop and deploy the first version of a model, workflow, dataset, or application in days or weeks, learn from real usage, and improve it iteratively. 

We are business-minded technologists who care more about impact than technical novelty. We use sophisticated methods when the problem requires them and simpler approaches when they will deliver a better result faster. Our work should be predictable, demoable, trusted, reusable, measured, and amplified by AI. 

 

About the role 

The Senior Data Scientist will build models, analyses, and supporting ML components that improve business decisions, intelligence products, and client outcomes. You will independently own defined deliverables—from understanding the requirement and preparing the data through modeling, validation, documentation, and delivery. 

This is a hands-on individual contributor role. You will work across varied revenue and intelligence initiatives, often in partnership with a Lead Data Scientist, application engineers, analysts, and business stakeholders. The right candidate can move quickly without sacrificing trustworthiness and knows how to balance statistical rigor with the practical needs of the business. 

 

What you’ll do

  • Own model and analysis deliverables. Take a defined business problem and independently deliver a reliable model, analysis component, scoring workflow, or supporting dataset.  

  • Translate business questions into analytical approaches. Ask clarifying questions, understand how the output will be used, and recommend an approach that fits the decision, timeline, and available data.  

  • Build and test models quickly. Develop practical solutions using statistical methods, machine learning, deep learning, or existing models and services where appropriate.  

  • Prepare trustworthy data. Profile, cleanse, join, and validate noisy datasets while checking completeness, freshness, distributions, nulls, duplicates, and match rates.  

  • Create repeatable scoring workflows. Move useful work beyond the notebook by building reusable Python components, batch-scoring processes, APIs, or lightweight services.  

  • Evaluate results responsibly. Establish baselines, select appropriate metrics, perform statistical reasonableness checks, reconcile unexpected results, and clearly document limitations.  

  • Support intelligence products and applications. Work with application and data teams to define the right data ingredients, test hypotheses, and integrate model outputs into usable experiences.  

  • Add operational discipline. Include validation, monitoring, failure handling, refresh expectations, documentation, and a clear usage path in delivered work.  

  • Use AI to improve your own productivity. Apply tools such as Claude, Codex, and similar assistants to accelerate coding, testing, research, debugging, and documentation while independently verifying the results.  

  • Communicate progress early and clearly. Make milestones, assumptions, risks, dependencies, and issues visible rather than waiting until delivery.  

 

What ownership looks like at this level

You are expected to own the deliverable. That means: 

  • Working independently on a well-defined model, workflow, dataset, or component  

  • Producing reliable and repeatable outputs rather than one-time analyses  

  • Adding appropriate validation and basic monitoring  

  • Documenting assumptions, methodology, limitations, and usage  

  • Demonstrating the output and explaining how it supports the business  

  • Raising risks and ambiguity early

jobs.title: Applied AI Engineer
jobs.jd: About Snowplow Snowplow is the real-time customer context layer that collects, validates, enriches, and delivers behavioral data for advanced analytics, ML, and AI agent decisioning. Snowplow 's event tracking is leveraged across 2M+ websites and applications globally, processing over one trillion events per month. More than 250 companies, including Experian, AutoTrader, Strava, Condé Nast, and HelloFresh, rely on Snowplow to build a well-governed, first-party data foundation that powers their customer-facing AI agents, in-session personalization and recommendations, and real-time analytics. This Opportunity Snowplow is rebuilding how the company runs its own work, and the Applied AI team owns Firn, the data and AI platform that work runs on, and the engineering standards that go with it. This role is an Applied AI engineer embedded with one business team, the way a site reliability engineer sits inside a product team: your line manager, your code reviewers and your career path come from Applied AI; your backlog and your day come from the team you serve. The Senior Director you report to still ships code. Your team is Growth, the group inside Marketing that books new meetings for our sellers. Its workflows already produce pipeline: an always-on outbound engine that scores accounts daily and sends hundreds of personalized sequences, a campaign builder that turns an AE's target list into a reviewed campaign, a morning routine that ranks warm contacts by intent signal, enrichment and signal pipelines from Apollo, Vector and reo.dev into Snowflake, and a paid-media loop that adjusts ads. They were built by people close to the work to get results fast, and they did. Now they need an engineer who makes them production grade and keeps them improving. You take over that estate, make it reliable, and make it better every week. The Director of Growth sets what matters, which is what moves pipeline now. You decide how it gets built and you build it. You work with our data engineers on scoring models and the semantic layer, with the platform engineer on the framework your workflows move onto, and with the Growth Associates and AEs who use what you ship. The engineering standards are Applied AI's; the tempo is Growth's. What you will own The GTM workflows in production. The outbound orchestrator and its sequences, the campaign builder, the intent-signal routine, the enrichment and signal pipelines, and the paid-media loop. You know how each one runs, what it costs, and what to do when it breaks. Review steps before anything sends. Agents that check the list, confirm each signal is current, and review the copy before a sequence goes out, with sampled human sign-off. The learning loop. Replies and meetings booked feed back into who we contact and what we say. You instrument the sends, run A/B tests on variants, and show the Growth team which messaging is working. Signals and enrichment. The pipelines that bring third-party signals and first-party behavior into Snowflake, the fields the Growth team needs exposed through our MCP tools, and the work with our data engineers that gets them there. Skills and routines for sellers. The Claude skills the Growth Associates and AEs run each morning, the campaign tooling, and the short working sessions that get a new team using them. Deliverability and suppression. One set of contact rules every sender reads, warm-inbox discipline, and the suppression windows that keep us welcome in people's inboxes. Engineering standards on your estate. Version control, alerting, tracing, runbooks and documented handover for every workflow you run, and a steady move of those workflows onto the Firn factory framework. The weekly cadence. A standing backlog with the Director of Growth, priorities set by pipeline, and a short written account of what shipped and what it did. When a priority and an engineering standard conflict, the Director of Growth and the Senior Director of Applied AI settle it together. We would love to hear from you if you have Written software that runs in production. Python and SQL are your working languages, you use git every day, and when you meet a new API you read the docs and use it. Tools like n8n, Clay or Zapier are in your kit, and when they run out you write the code. Built with LLMs for real work. Prompts, tools, structured outputs and evaluation, and the failure modes of each. You know what a model does when a prompt does not say where to get its data, and you design against it. Run something that could not go down. Alerting, error handling, retries and recovery are habits, and when something does fail you fix the class of problem, not the instance. Moved data into a warehouse. You have built or maintained pipelines into Snowflake or an equivalent, and you can model a table in dbt or learn to quickly. Sat with sellers and marketers. You can take a growth director's ask, work out what they need, and come back with something they use the next week. When an ask is a symptom of a broken process, you say so before you build it. A fast tempo. The team you serve measures in meetings booked per week. You are measured on what you build: whether it runs, what it costs, and what it changed for the team. You ship small, measure, and say plainly when something is not working. An AI-native way of working you can show us. A workflow, automation or agent you built and still use. Expect to demonstrate it during the interview process. Comfort being embedded. You can sit inside another team, take its priorities, and still hold the engineering standards your own team sets. Bonus points for Experience with Salesforce, Apollo, Smartlead, Lemlist or similar GTM tooling and their APIs. Experience with email deliverability at volume. Experience with paid-media platform APIs. How we hire for this role The interview process includes a short technical exercise in code and a working session where you walk us through how you work with AI on a real task, using your own setup. jobs.jd: About the Organization Now is a great time to join Redhorse Corporation. We are a solution-driven company delivering data insights and technology solutions to customers with missions critical to U.S. national interests. We’re looking for thoughtful, skilled professionals who thrive as trusted partners building technology-agnostic solutions and want to apply their talents supporting customers with difficult and important mission sets. About the Role Redhorse transforms the way government uses data and technology. To support this mission, we are seeking an Artificial Intelligence (AI)/Machine Learning (ML) Engineer to support Condition-Based Maintenance Plus (CBM+) initiatives that improve aircraft sustainment and optimize maintenance and logistics for the United States Air Force (USAF). In this role, you will serve as a key architect in the CBM+ ecosystem, bridging the gap between cutting-edge development and operational deployment. Working within cross-functional teams in an Agile environment, you will translate complex predictive models into production-grade systems that directly enhance fleet readiness and sustainment efficiency. This is a unique opportunity to operate at the intersection of aerospace logistics and advanced MLOps, delivering high-impact solutions for our nation's defense. Key Responsibilities Lead CBM+ AI/ML initiatives from concept through production deployment, ensuring technical solutions align with mission outcomes, business objectives, and enterprise architecture standards. Architect and oversee scalable data pipelines, including data ingestion, ETL/ELT processing, feature engineering, data validation, and sustainment of production data workflows. Design, develop, and optimize machine learning, deep learning, and generative AI models to solve complex operational problems and improve predictive maintenance capabilities. Perform advanced exploratory data analysis, statistical modeling, and data visualization to uncover trends, correlations, risk indicators, and actionable insights that guide product and mission decisions. Build, maintain, and extend knowledge graph capabilities to support semantic reasoning, data integration, and AI-enabled decision support. Provide technical leadership to multi-functional engineering teams, mentoring junior engineers and guiding best practices for model development, MLOps, testing, documentation, and secure deployment. Collaborate with software, data, cloud, and product teams to integrate trained models into production applications, APIs, and operational workflows. Establish monitoring strategies for data quality, model performance, drift, bias, and degradation, and lead mitigation efforts to maintain reliable AI/ML system performance. Required Experience/Clearance An active Secret security clearance is mandatory for this position. Applicants must currently possess an active Secret clearance to be considered. Candidates without an active clearance will not be considered. Education & Experience: Master’s degree in a STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering, or Mathematics) field or proven equivalent professional experience. Natural Language Processing (NLP): Minimum of 5 years of experience incorporating applied NLP, data labeling, and entity or keyword extraction. Analytics & Data Engineering: Proven proficiency with Databricks, PySpark, SQL, data governance frameworks, and technical documentation standards. Statistical Foundations: Deep understanding and practical application of statistical distributions for data assessment, data analysis, and predictive modeling. Visualization & Data Products: Experience developing dashboard or data end-products utilizing tools such as Streamlit, Qlik Sense, or similar platforms. Tools & Methodologies: Experience using project management and productivity platforms including Jira, Confluence, Lucidchart, and Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint). Communication & Initiative: Demonstrated self-starter with strong interpersonal skills, with the proven ability to translate complex technical findings for executive and non-technical stakeholders. Travel: Ability to travel minimally as needed to engage with government customers and project stakeholders. Desired Experience We encourage all candidates who meet the basic requirements to apply, even if you do not have any of the following experience: Ph.D. in a STEM field, with a preference for Data Science, Data Analytics, or Computer Science. Advanced expertise applying artificial intelligence and machine learning (AI/ML) to predictive maintenance, condition-based maintenance, or defense logistics challenges. Direct experience developing sensor-based failure prediction models and equipment health indicators. Practical experience conducting Monte Carlo simulations and calculating statistical confidence intervals. Demonstrated expertise in end-to-end data pipeline engineering, including customer-facing UI/UX integration. Prior experience supporting defense aviation data environments or DoD enterprise systems. The salary range provided for this position represents the anticipated base salary for successful candidates. Actual compensation will be determined based on a variety of factors, including relevant experience, education, certifications, skills, security clearance level, geographic location, market conditions, and internal equity. In addition to base salary, eligible employees may participate in Redhorse 's comprehensive benefits programs and may be eligible for performance-based or other incentive compensation, where applicable. jobs.title: Data Scientist (Fraud)
jobs.jd: Who we are Ranked in 2024 by the Financial Times, Moniepoint is Africa’s fastest-growing fintech, trusted by over 10 million business and individual accounts, processing billions of Naira in transactions monthly. Our mission is to enable financial happiness for every African, everywhere. About this role: We're looking for a Data Scientist to sit at the heart of how we fight fraud — building the models, experiments, and detection systems that protect millions of customers and merchants across our platform. This is a high-impact role at the intersection of machine learning, product, and engineering, where your work will directly shape how Moniepoint detects and responds to emerging fraud threats. You are a data-driven, intellectually curious Data Scientist who is energized by hard problems in fraud and financial crime. You'll prototype and ship ML models, design experiments, and uncover new fraud signals across our ecosystem — partnering closely with engineers, product managers, and analysts to turn your work into production-grade systems. Responsibilities: Prototype, evaluate, and help produce machine learning models for fraud detection; own their ongoing monitoring and retraining cycles. Design and run experiments to measure the impact of fraud interventions, balancing customer experience against loss reduction. Size fraud typologies across our product lines to inform prioritization and investment decisions. Build and maintain anomaly detection systems to surface novel fraud vectors before they scale. Work closely with fraud operations, engineers, product managers, and data analysts to translate model outputs into real-world mitigations. Experience & Background: A strong foundation in statistics with a degree in a quantitative field (Statistics, Mathematics, Engineering, Computer Science, or similar). 3+ years of experience in data science, decision science, or risk analytics within fraud, payments, or financial crime. Hands-on experience building and deploying machine learning models in a production environment. Fraud, risk, or financial services experience is a strong plus. Solid grounding in data science fundamentals: experimentation, statistical inference, model evaluation, and feature engineering. Comfort working in fast-paced, cross-functional teams with high ownership expectations. Skills & Competencies: Proficiency in Python and SQL; comfort working across the full model development lifecycle. An investigative instinct — you enjoy digging into data to find patterns others miss. The ability to communicate technical findings clearly to non-technical stakeholders and translate insights into action. What Success Looks Like in This Role: Production-grade ML models and anomaly detection systems that effectively surface and mitigate novel fraud vectors before they scale. Well-designed experiments that successfully balance customer experience against fraud loss reduction. Clear sizing of fraud typologies that effectively drives product prioritization and strategic investment decisions. Seamless cross-functional alignment where technical model outputs are consistently translated into real-world fraud mitigations. Why Join Us? Culture: We put our people first and prioritize the well-being of every team member. We've built a company where all opinions carry weight and where all voices are heard. We value and respect each other and always look out for one another. Above all, we are human. Learning: We have a learning and development-focused environment with an emphasis on knowledge sharing, training, and regular internal technical talks. Compensation: You'll receive an attractive salary, pension, health insurance, annual bonus, plus other benefits. Moniepoint is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees and candidates. Originally posted on Himalayas

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer, GPU Code Generation for Machine Learning Inference
jobs.jd: NVIDIA is seeking talented engineers to join the TensorRT team and advance high-performance AI inference on NVIDIA GPUs. Our team develops software that accelerates state-of-the-art generative AI models for local and enterprise deployments. We solve challenging problems in GPU code generation, just-in-time compilation, and inference optimization to deliver high performance across diverse models and hardware configurations. As a Senior Software Engineer, you will develop advanced GPU inference software for TensorRT. We’re looking for engineers with strong experience in GPU optimization and compiler development who can translate a deep understanding of GPU execution into efficient code generation and measurable improvements in generative AI inference. What you’ll be doing: Design and implement efficient GPU code generation techniques in TensorRT that balance generated code performance, compilation overhead, and startup latency. Develop compiler optimizations, including operator fusion, dynamic scheduling, and specialization for model shapes, data types, and GPU architectures. Profile workloads and analyze generated GPU code to identify bottlenecks and guide compiler and runtime improvements. Develop robust, maintainable software in C++, and Python for tooling, testing, and performance analysis. Collaborate with GPU architects, kernel developers, compiler engineers, and deep learning experts to guide hardware and software design. What we need to see: BS, MS, or PhD in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent experience. 4+ years of relevant software development experience, including contributions to a substantial codebase or project. Strong proficiency in C++ and experience building performance-critical software. Understanding of GPU architecture and parallel programming concepts, including memory hierarchies, thread execution, synchronization, and resource utilization. A rigorous approach to performance analysis and debugging, with the ability to validate numerical correctness and explain performance tradeoffs. Strong problem-solving and communication skills, and the ability to work independently and collaborate across teams. Ways to stand out from the crowd: Experience developing or optimizing GPU kernels using CUDA, Triton, CuTe DSL, CUTLASS, or other GPU programming languages. Experience with MLIR compiler infrastructure, familiarity with intermediate representations, lowering, optimization passes, and GPU code generation. Familiarity with NVIDIA Tensor Core architecture, mixed-precision computation, quantization, or low-level GPU performance analysis using tools such as NVIDIA Nsight. Experience developing inference frameworks such as PyTorch, JAX, ONNX Runtime, TensorRT, TensorRT-LLM, vLLM, and SGLang. A track record of measurable performance improvements in production software or contributions to GPU programming and compiler projects. At NVIDIA , you’ll work with engineers across GPU architecture, compilers, and AI software to solve demanding performance problems. If you are curious and enjoy understanding how hardware executes code and building software that pushes its capabilities, join us in shaping the future of generative AI inference. Your base salary will be determined based on your location, experience, and other objective job-related factors. The expected base salary ranges for this position are: 152,000 USD – 241,500 USD for Level 3; and 184,000 USD – 287,500 USD for Level 4. You will also be eligible for equity and benefits. Applications for this job will be accepted at least until November 3, 2026. This posting is for an existing vacancy. NVIDIA uses AI tools in its recruiting processes. NVIDIA is committed to fostering an inclusive work environment and proud to be an equal opportunity employer. jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer (Agentic Search) – Web Rendering (Chromium)
jobs.jd:
About Nebius:

Nebius is leading a new era in cloud infrastructure for the global AI economy. We are building a full-stack AI cloud platform that supports developers and enterprises from data and model training through to production deployment, without the cost and complexity of building large in-house AI/ML infrastructure.

Built by engineers, for engineers. From large-scale GPU orchestration to inference optimization, we own the hard problems across compute, storage, networking and applied AI.

Listed on Nasdaq (NBIS) and headquartered in Amsterdam, we have a global footprint with R&D hubs across Europe, the UK, North America and Israel. Our team of 1,500+ includes hundreds of engineers with deep expertise across hardware, software and AI R&D.

The Product

In a rapidly evolving world, trust in AI depends on AI agents being grounded in fresh, verified real-world data. Search is the foundation that makes this possible. We are building an agent-native search platform designed specifically for AI systems rather than human users. Our product provides programmatic, low-latency, and observable search APIs that AI agents use to retrieve, filter, and reason over real-world information at scale.

The Role

We are looking for a Senior Software Engineer to work on the rendering infrastructure of a novel search engine tailored for agentic AI consumption.

In this role, you will focus on loading modern web pages in a browser that we patch and build ourselves, so that content is rendered completely and reliably at a cost that works across billions of pages. You will work inside Chromium to remove what we do not need, make the rest faster and cheaper, and keep our build current as Chromium moves. Your work ensures that high-quality content is consistently available to the indexing and retrieval systems downstream.

In this position, your responsibility will be to

  • Change Chromium in its heavy core (Blink, the V8 integration, the compositor, the network service) to cut CPU, memory and startup cost per page
  • Strip Chromium down for agent workloads: skip what nobody needs, such as image and media decoding, web font downloads, and rasterization and GPU work where no one needs pixels, while keeping what page scripts depend on to run correctly (style, layout, animation frames, observers), and work out what breaks, or renders differently, when you do
  • Keep the browser compatible with the web: make sure that what we remove does not change how the sites we load behave or render
  • Profile and tune fleets of browsers: the process model, memory per renderer, startup, isolation and crash handling
  • Build the production system around it: how browsers are launched, pooled, recycled and monitored

You may be a good fit if you

Have 5+ years of experience building production systems, and are an expert in several of the following areas.

Inside the browser

  • Strong C++ in a large, performance-critical codebase, ideally Chromium, Blink or V8, or a comparable browser engine (Rust is a plus)
  • Chromium architecture: the process model, Mojo IPC, the rendering pipeline (DOM, style, layout, paint, compositing), and the network service
  • Building, debugging and shipping custom Chromium builds: the build system, tracing, crash analysis, and maintaining patches across releases

Performance and systems

  • Profiling CPU, memory and I/O for browser fleets, with tools such as perf, tracing and flame graphs
  • Linux process isolation and resource management, concurrency, and memory management
  • Have run browsers in production, or built the infrastructure that does, and can describe where the time and memory went

Strong candidates may also have experience with

  • Contributions to Chromium, Blink, V8, Firefox, WebKit or another browser engine
  • Building or maintaining a patched browser that you wrote the patches for
  • Browser instrumentation, including the Chrome DevTools Protocol
  • Working familiarity with how modern frontend frameworks render (SSR, CSR, streaming, hydration)
  • Distributed systems, Kubernetes, and Go or Python

The kind of problems you will work on

  • Cut the cost of loading a page in half. Where do CPU and memory go, and what would you change in the browser?
  • Turn off the GPU and image decoding for agent workloads. What breaks, and what changes in how pages load and render?
  • A page runs a script that never yields. How do we detect and stop it without help from the page?
  • Chromium ships a new version. How do we bring a large set of patches forward in days, not weeks?
  • Decide when a page is finished, for pages with analytics beacons, long polling and endless scrolling.

We conduct coding interviews as part of the process.

Benefits & Perks:

  • Competitive compensation
  • Career growth and learning opportunities
  • Flexibility and ownership
  • Collaborative and innovative culture
  • Opportunity to work on impactful AI projects
  • International environment and talented teams

What's it like to work at Nebius:

Fast moving - Bold thinking - Constant growth - Meaningful impact - Trust and real ownership - Opportunity to shape the future of AI

We give technical teams the freedom of code with the speed of no-code, so they can automate faster, smarter, and without limits. Backed by a fiercely inventive community and 500+ builder-approved integrations, we’re changing the way people bring systems together and scale ideas for impact. Since our founding in 2019, we’ve grown into a diverse team of over 260 - working across Europe and the US, connected by a shared builder spirit and with our centre of gravity in Berlin. Along the way, we’ve: Cultivated a community of more than 650,000 active developers and builders Earned 190K+ GitHub stars, making us one of the world’s Top 40 most popular projects Backed by top investors, from Sequoia’s first German seed to our SAP's recent strategic investment - bringing us to a $5.2bn valuation That’s the company we’ve built. jobs.title: Senior Data Scientist (AI, ML, Pyspark, SQL)
jobs.jd: Our Purpose Mastercard powers economies and empowers people in 200+ countries and territories worldwide. Together with our customers, we’re helping build a sustainable economy where everyone can prosper. We support a wide range of digital payments choices, making transactions secure, simple, smart and accessible. Our technology and innovation, partnerships and networks combine to deliver a unique set of products and services that help people, businesses and governments realize their greatest potential. Title and Summary Senior Data Scientist (AI, ML, Pyspark, SQL) Overview The Business & Market Insights (B&MI) team within Mastercard's Services division creates products that help customers including financial institutions and merchants understand their customers and the market better. The B&MI Data Science team uses data from Mastercard transactions and other sources to build models and solutions that are needed for these products, at a globally scalable level across the different customer lifecycle stages. This role is for a Data Scientist that will work across Product, Client Services & Delivery, Data & Engineering and the broader teams, to deliver truly differentiated products driven by analytics & AI, leveraging rich data resources, AI platform capabilities and near real-time execution. We are developing multiple new products and capabilities using analytics & AI, and this role is central in that vision, from concept, technical design to market release and optimization. This role is positioned to drive new ideas forward by combining creative thought leadership with innovation and industry best practices. By entering in the early phase of a truly transformative and impactful strategic initiative, the experience is certain to be rewarding. This role requires the successful candidate to have the following: - 5-9 years of overall career experience in Data Science function supporting Products - Design, develop, and productionize machine learning and data science solutions that solve complex business problems within BMI. - Develop traditional ML solutions covering feature engineering, model training, validation, evaluation, and deployment. - Perform exploratory data analysis and translate complex datasets into actionable insights. - Optimize data pipelines and ML workflows for performance, scalability, maintainability, and reliability. - Develop robust and reusable Python components following sound software-engineering practices. - Use PySpark to process, transform, and analyze large datasets efficiently in distributed environments. - Write advanced, optimized SQL for data extraction, transformation, feature development, and analytical workloads. - Apply appropriate controls for data privacy, security, responsible AI, monitoring, and explainability. Good to have: - Understanding of building Generative AI applications using Python and modern GenAI frameworks. The successful candidate’s primary responsibilities will be to: - Drive the evolution of Business & Market Insights products by applying Data Science and Artificial Intelligence to create models, tools and capabilities - Participate in the exploration, application and development of data science for product development - Participate in identification and evaluation of AI/ML techniques and tools to deliver models and analytics for product development - Continuously innovate and determine new data science approaches & technologies to solve business problems and generate business insights & recommendations - Partner with roles across the organization including product, engineering, and sales to determine the highest priority data science problems to solve in a customer-centric framework - Evaluate trade-offs between many possible analytics solutions to a problem, taking into account performance, usability, technical feasibility, timelines, and differing stakeholder opinions to make a decision - Break large solutions into smaller, releasable milestones to collect data and feedback from product managers, clients and other stakeholders - Evangelize releases to users, incorporating feedback, and tracking usage to inform future development - Work with small, cross-functional teams to define vision, establish team culture and processes - Consistently focus on key drivers of organization value and prioritize operational activities accordingly - Identify and act upon product improvement opportunities - Provide technical leadership of junior colleagues as a senior member of the data science team, through technical and non-technical mentoring Corporate Security Responsibility All activities involving access to Mastercard assets, information, and networks comes with an inherent risk to the organization and, therefore, it is expected that every person working for, or on behalf of, Mastercard is responsible for information security and must: Abide by Mastercard’s security policies and practices; Ensure the confidentiality and integrity of the information being accessed; Report any suspected information security violation or breach, and Complete all periodic mandatory security trainings in accordance with Mastercard’s guidelines.

jobs.title: Expert Data Scientist, Fraud Risk Detection
jobs.jd: Overview Experian's Fraud Analytics & Commercialization operates across four main functions. These include client engagement analytics, scalable and custom analytics for financial institutions, fraud analytics consulting, and solution integrity and enablement for production-ready platforms. We're looking for a motivated Data Scientist to help build fraud detection models and features that identify high-risk activity while minimizing friction for legitimate customers. Core skills for this role include an eagerness to collaborate, and empathy. You will will dig into surprising signals in the data and to learn how that insight becomes a deployed model. You will help investigate the latest fraud patterns, build features, and train and evaluate machine learning models. You will work with senior data scientists and engineers starting with problem definition through feature engineering, experimentation, and deployment. You will be a developing programmer, ready to translate theoretical principles into production-ready solutions. We continue to sharpen through research and the engineering that turns those findings into tools and systems built for commercialization. This is a remote role and you will report into the Sr. Manager of Fraud Analytics. What you'll do Investigate large datasets, including exploratory analysis and fraud label development, to identify latest fraud patterns, attack methods, and behavioral signals. Translate ambiguous fraud and risk problems into clear hypotheses, analytical plans, model requirements, and measurable success criteria. Develop machine learning models for fraud detection across account opening, account takeover, and identity risk. Evaluate models using metrics like ROC/AUC/KS/Gini, precision/recall, fraud capture rate, false-positive rate, customer friction, and fraud losses prevented. Develop and validate predictive features using identity, transactional, consumer credit history, device, behavioral, temporal, velocity, network, and third-party data. Write clean, efficient, well-tested Python and PySpark code, and collaborate with teams to bring models and features into batch, retro, or real-time decisioning environments. Monitor feature quality, model performance, population changes, and fraud-pattern drift Design and present analyses for model behavior, tradeoffs, risks, and recommendations Follow appropriate standards for data privacy, model documentation, explainability, validation, and governance. Qualifications At least 5 years of experience in data science, machine learning, statistical modeling, or a related quantitative field Bachelor's or advanced degree in computer science, statistics, engineering, data science, or another quantitative discipline Direct experience developing fraud-detection, identity-risk, credit-risk, financial-crime, or other adversarial risk models. Demonstrated experience creating meaningful fraud features Proficiency in Python and PySpark, with experience writing modular and tested code for large datasets and distributed or cloud data systems. Experience using common data science and machine-learning tools such as pandas, NumPy, scikit-learn, XGBoost, TensorFlow, or comparable technologies. Knowledge of supervised learning, model evaluation, feature selection, statistical inference, experimentation, and model calibration. Experience navigating challenges common to fraud modeling, including class imbalance, delayed or incomplete labels, changing attack patterns, and model drift. Experience moving models beyond experimentation and into production, either directly or in close partnership with engineering teams. #LI-Remote Benefits/Perks: Great compensation package and bonus plan Core benefits including medical, dental, vision, and matching 401K Flexible work environment, ability to work remote, hybrid or in-office Flexible time off including volunteer time off, vacation, sick and 12-paid holidays Explore all our exciting benefits here: https://yourexperianbenefits.com/cand-index.html Our uniqueness is that we celebrate yours. Experian's people first, inclusive and purpose-driven culture is multi award-winning. We have won World's Best Workplaces™ 2025 (Fortune Global Top 25), and Great Place To Work™ in 26 countries to name a few. Experian's recruitment process is conducted only through authorised channels. Recruitment communications will only be sent from an @ experian.com email address. Experian will never ask candidates to make any payment as part of a recruitment process. Our compensation reflects the cost of labor across several U.S. geographic markets. Within this range, individual pay is determined by work location and additional factors such as job-related skills, experience, and education. You will be eligible for a variable pay opportunity and a comprehensive benefits package. If you have a disability or special need that requires accommodation, please let us know at the earliest opportunity.

of our personalisation and player engagement capabilities, including our Next Best Action engine and propensity modelling programme You will have helped shape the roadmap for new AI product opportunities, drawing on a clear view of where ML and agent-based approaches can generate near-term value for the business Essential: At least 3 years’ experience in an applied Data Science or ML role, with a track record of shipping models or AI products into production Demonstrated ability to deliver measurable outcomes through applied ML: your work has made it into the hands of end users, jobs.title: Data Scientist - H/F/NB
jobs.jd: En nous rejoignant sur ce poste, vous intégrerez une équipe multidisciplinaire (data, programmation, game & narrative design, animation, etc.), guidée par une question simple et ambitieuse : parmi toutes les possibilités offertes par l’IA générative, lesquelles sont réellement intéressantes et fun pour le gameplay ? L’équipe a pour mission de tester de nouvelles expériences auprès de joueurs et joueuses, et d’équiper les créateur·rices pour imaginer des interactions plus dynamiques, immersives et surprenantes — jusqu’à faire émerger des features impossibles à réaliser autrement. Son quotidien s’inscrit à la croisée de la R&D, du développement produit, de la création de jeux courts et de la collaboration multi-studios, au service des gameplays de demain. Dans le cadre de ce poste, vous rejoindrez une équipe développant un produit technologique favorisant l'intégration de l’IA au sein des fonctionnalités de nos jeux. Au sein de nos studios de production, vous pourrez apporter vos connaissances en Data Science afin de construire des expériences de jeux uniques. Missions Au sein de l’équipe du produit technologique intégrant l’IA générative dans nos gameplays, vous apportez vos connaissances en Data Science et Machine Learning afin de prototyper et modéliser des solutions permettant la création de nouvelles expériences de jeu: Identifier des objectifs en fonction des spécifications partagées par les équipes de design et à travers l’analyse des données joueurs et définir des protocoles d’évaluation Concevoir des prototypes et entrainer des modèles pour répondre à ces objectifs Collaborer avec les Machine Learning Engineers pour transférer les prototypes et définir les critères de succès en vue de leur intégration. Collaborer avec les designers pour analyser les comportements de vos IA et identifier des pistes d’améliorations du jeu. Identifier les opportunités d’expérimentation et d’innovation. Communiquer sur vos travaux et vos résultats de façon pédagogique pour un public varié. Vous disposez au moins d’une première expérience significative en tant que Data Scientist, durant laquelle vous avez pu mener des projets sur des produits interactifs (jeux, apps, systèmes temps réel …), Vous avez une bonne maitrise de Python ainsi que Tensorflow ou PyTorch (avoir une expérience en pyspark est un +), Vous disposez de solides bases en statistiques et méthodes d’évaluation (analyse exploratoire, tests statistiques, A/B testing), Vous êtes à l’aise avec l’analyse de données complexes et séquentielles issues de systèmes interactifs et avez de bonnes connaissances des LLM , Vous êtes une personne dotée d’une bonne capacité d’écoute, de compréhension et vous savez traduire les besoins des clients en spécifications , Vous faites preuve d’autonomie et de curiosité et avez un véritable intérêt pour le jeu vidéo. Enfin, votre maîtrise de l’anglais vous permet d’être à l’aise dans les échanges écrits et oraux avec des interlocuteurs de différents pays. En tant qu’employeur, Ubisoft offre à tous les mêmes opportunités d’accès à l’emploi, sans distinction notamment de genre, ethnicité, religion, orientation sexuelle, statut social, handicap et d’âge. Ubisoft veille à développer un environnement de travail inclusif qui reflète la diversité de sa communauté de joueurs dans ses équipes.

jobs.jd: View our much better version of this job spec on our careers page: https://juro.notion.site/aie *** THE KEY BITS Location : We can currently only accept applications from candidates that are located and have long-term working rights in the UK. Flexibility : We have office hubs in London and Boston, as well as no-office hubs in several European countries. We operate a choice-first work approach that lets you work fully remotely from Day One even if you’re near an office hub. Salary : We benchmarked £115,000 + equity at IC4 level in our progression framework for someone based in the UK. What you’ve done in the last ~2 years is far more important to us than how long you’ve been an engineer — so if you think you meet the requirements but are worried you’re not “senior” enough, we strongly encourage you to still apply. If you like the look of the role but the salary doesn’t match what you’re looking for, let us know in your application. Interviews : 3 stages totalling around 3 hours over 2-3 weeks. Start date : As soon as you can start. Reporting to : Pavel Nekrasov , Director of Engineering and lead of the Agentic team at Juro More info : The FAQ below, juro.com/careers , our handbook or ask ----- anything. HELP US HELP THE WORLD AGREE FASTER Juro has big ambitions: to make it incredibly easy for anyone to agree and manage legal contracts. And we'll need help doing it . Legal tech is on the rise, with Goldman Sachs estimating that 44% of legal tasks can be automated with generative AI. With the brand we have built and the agility of early stage we are well placed to capture this opportunity. Our Agentic team was the first team at Juro to go fully AI-native, and it's been the role model for our other product teams as Juro evolved into an AI company. As the Agentic team, we build the AI foundations the rest of engineering ships on — starting with Operator , the agent that works across contracts inside Juro. We want Operator to do a lot more. That takes more and better tools, solid evals, and a harness that keeps up with a stack that’s still rapidly evolving. And more great people to do it. What you're here to do Give Operator the tools it needs to act across Juro and make sure what it does is measurably good. In your first months, success looks like this: You've shipped new tools that connect Operator to the Juro app, from first idea to production. What you ship has evals around it, supported by the Quality Assurance team, so we can tell whether a new model, prompt or library version makes things better or worse. You own parts of the agent harness (planning, tool use, context) without the team becoming a. bottleneck. You review a lot of agent-written code and decide quickly what's safe to merge and what will break three cycles later. We care about building a diverse team where everyone feels they belong. That’s why our perks & benefits and choice-first work approach are designed with inclusivity in mind. Read more in our diversity, inclusion & belonging hub . WHO WE LOOK FOR Research shows that while men apply to jobs if they meet ~60% of criteria, women and those in traditionally under-represented groups tend to apply only if they check all boxes. So if you think you have what it takes but don't meet every single point above, please still get in touch. We'd love to have a chat and see if you could be a great fit. To succeed here: Every Juror finds their balance across our four core Principles — we hire, develop and celebrate people who live them every day. Curious how you’d fit? Try our personality quiz to see how you map against our principles. On top of that, you have been part of a journey where: You’re a programmer first, and you now build with AI and LLMs. You’ve written production TypeScript/Node.js and MongoDB for users. Agents write most of the code today, but you can still tell when an agent’s output shouldn’t go through. You’ve built agentic systems yourself, including the tools that let agents act on APIs and integrations. You can explain the parts of an agent (planning, tools, context, the loop around them) because you’ve built them. You’ve written and run evals and think about quality in probabilities. You’ve shipped something people can use: a product, an open-source project or a tool. (We’ll ask you for a link or description in our application form.) Bonus: you’ve used our AI stack before. It changes often, so understanding why things break matters more than knowing the tools already. Day to day, you’ll work with Node.js , TypeScript , MongoDB , Redis and pgvector on AWS , plus Bedrock , LiteLLM and Mastra for the AI layer. These requirements can come from a job, a side project or open source. The field is about two years old, so we care about what you've built, not how many years you've been doing it. This job likely isn’t for you if: You need a polished setup before you can ship. We'd rather ship a small, good version this week than a perfect one in two weeks, by which time the stack has moved on. You want a stable roadmap. Priorities here can change week to week. You want to rebuild things whenever you'd have done them differently. We disagree a lot and openly, but once a call is made, we commit and move. You've only ever worked inside one opinionated framework and never looked under the hood. You'd rather build product UI. Most of this work is foundations other engineers build on. OUR MISSION Juro exists to help the world agree faster by making it incredibly easy for anyone to agree and manage legal contracts. The load on legal teams is increasing as business teams move faster with the help of AI. The only way out is to deploy AI within the legal team so that (a) routine contract work can be executed autonomously and (b) lawyers’ time is reserved for problem solving. It’s like having an extra team member that is always on and takes on heavy lifting. Just like an in-house lawyer, Juro: is present for, and trusted by, business teams owns contracts from first draft to signatur

jobs.title: Data Scientist, Enterprise Analytics
jobs.jd:
GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.

The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. Co-create the future with us as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.

*Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.

An Overview of this role

As a Data Scientist at GitLab on the Enterprise Analytics team,  you’ll be a trusted analytical partner to Sales, Revenue Operations, and Finance, helping define how we measure go-to-market performance and where we invest to grow. This is a strategic and hands-on role. You’ll apply statistical, experimentation, and machine learning methods to forecast outcomes, explain what drives activation, conversion, expansion, and retention, and size opportunities. You’ll also support the company-level reporting and GTM performance views that executives use to run the business, covering consumption, ARR, and first orders.

What you’ll do

  • Embed yourself with business teams to become a trusted partner supporting insight generation and strategic decision making across GTM.
  • Perform exploratory data analysis to uncover behavioral trends, long-term patterns, and the key drivers and levers behind business performance, and communicate their impact clearly to non-technical audiences.
  • Build and productionize machine learning models - such as propensity, product-qualified lead (PQL) scoring, churn, and expansion models - including training, validation, testing, and feature engineering, using MLOps practices and tooling (CI/CD for ML pipelines, model registries, automated retraining, and monitoring) to move work reliably from notebook to production
  • Design, run, and evaluate growth experiments (A/B tests and quasi-experiments) on onboarding, pricing and packaging, and upgrade flows, and measure their impact on activation, conversion, and retention
  • Build and operationalize agentic workflows for analysis, modeling, and pipeline automation, with evaluation and monitoring that keep agent-generated insights accurate, traceable, and trustworthy.
  • Contribute to GitLab’s Semantic Layer enabling stakeholders and agents to self-serve metrics using trusts and tested sources.
  • Write production-grade Python and SQL that meets internal standards for style, maintainability, and performance in a high-scale database environment; maintain and advocate for these standards through code review

What you’ll bring

  • 3-5 years of professional experience in GTM analytics, data science, or a similar technical role
  • Demonstrated ability to translate ambiguous business problems into clear, measurable questions and communicate technical concepts effectively to non-technical stakeholders.
  • Experience with experimentation and causal inference (A/B testing, power analysis, quasi-experimental methods) and with statistical and machine learning methods such as regression, classification, clustering, and survival analysis
  • Deep, hands-on understanding of SQL in cloud data warehouses (like Snowflake SQL), including working with product usage and event data, and in business intelligence tools (Looker, Tableau, Hex, or similar)
  • Experience using Python for statistical modeling, machine learning, and production data science. With hands-on experience in pandas, NumPy, scikit-learn, Jupyter, and related libraries such as LightGBM and XGBoost
  • Hands-on experience building agentic workflows with AI coding agents (e.g., Claude Code, OpenCode, or similar), including connecting agents to the right context, tools, and platforms such as MLflow, and evaluating their output for accuracy and reliability.
  • Experience working in a B2C company working with motions and metrics, including Consumption, CRR, ARR, and Churn & Contraction
  • Self-motivated and self-managing, with strong organizational skills
  • Ability to use GitLab and to thrive in a fully remote organization

About the Team

The Enterprise Analytics team builds the trusted data products and insights behind GitLab’s Company wide sales, revenue, and finance reporting. We work across the business on metrics including First Orders, pipeline, CRR, ARR, and other key indicators, helping leaders make informed decisions and teams understand how their work contributes to GitLab’s growth.

We support a wide range of digital payments choices, making transactions secure, simple, smart and accessible. Our technology and innovation, partnerships and networks combine to deliver a unique set of products and services that help people, businesses and governments realize their greatest potential. Title and Summary Senior AI Engineer Overview Mastercard's AI Centre of Excellence is building the next generation of AI capabilities powered by large-scale transaction data, machine learning, and foundation models. We are transforming how AI solutions are developed by enabling teams to leverage reusable learned intelligence rather than building bespoke feature-engineering pipelines for every use case. We are seeking a Senior Data Scientist, AI Engineering to develop advanced machine learning solutions across domains. This role combines deep expertise in predictive modelling, experimentation, and applied machine learning to deliver measurable business impact. The successful candidate will partner closely with engineering, product, and business teams to bring innovative AI solutions from concept to production. What You'll Work On This role focuses on applying machine learning, predictive modelling, and foundation-model representations to solve business problems at scale. Typical use cases include forecasting, propensity modelling, recommendation systems, behavioural analytics, and customer intelligence. While familiarity with Generative AI is beneficial, this is primarily an applied machine learning and data science role rather than a conversational AI, RAG, or agentic systems engineering position. Role / Key Responsibilities Design, develop, and deploy machine learning solutions that solve high-impact business problems. Define modelling approaches, experimentation methodologies, and success metrics for AI initiatives. Apply foundation-model embeddings and modern machine learning techniques to improve model performance and accelerate development. Drive projects from problem definition through model development, deployment, and impact measurement. Develop robust evaluation frameworks and benchmark new approaches against existing solutions. Partner with business, product, engineering, and analytics teams to identify and prioritise opportunities. Communicate technical findings and recommendations to both technical and non-technical stakeholders. Contribute to the development of best practices, reusable assets, and modelling standards across the AI organisation. Support and mentor junior data scientists through technical guidance and knowledge sharing. All About You Required Experience Proven experience developing and deploying machine learning solutions in production environments. Experience solving predictive modelling problems such as attrition, forecasting, recommendation systems, propensity modelling, fraud detection, risk modelling, or customer analytics. Strong track record of delivering measurable business outcomes through machine learning. Experience working in cross-functional teams to bring data science solutions from concept to deployment. Required Technical Skills Strong expertise in machine learning, predictive analytics, statistical modelling, and experimentation. Advanced Python and SQL skills. Experience with machine learning frameworks such as Scikit-Learn, XGBoost, LightGBM, TensorFlow, or PyTorch. Strong understanding of classification, regression, forecasting, recommendation systems, ranking, clustering, and anomaly detection. Experience with feature engineering, representation learning, embeddings, and downstream machine learning workflows. Familiarity with transformer-based models and foundation-model applications. Experience working with Databricks, Spark, Azure, AWS, or GCP. Leadership & Communication Strong analytical problem-solving skills. Ability to influence stakeholders through technical expertise and data-driven recommendations. Excellent communication and collaboration skills. Ability to translate complex technical concepts into actionable business insights. Minimum Qualifications Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Statistics, Mathematics, Engineering, or a related quantitative field. 5+ years of experience in machine learning, data science, AI, or advanced analytics. Experience developing and deploying machine learning models in production environments. Demonstrated experience applying statistical and machine learning techniques to real-world business problems. Preferred Qualifications Master's degree or PhD in Machine Learning, Artificial Intelligence, Computer Science, Statistics, Mathematics, or a related field. Experience with foundation models, embeddings, or representation learning. Experience in financial services, payments, banking, fintech, fraud, marketing analytics, or customer intelligence. Publications, patents, conference presentations, or other evidence of technical thought leadership. Corporate Security Responsibility All activities involving access to Mastercard assets, information, and networks comes with an inherent risk to the organization and, therefore, it is expected that every person working for, or on behalf of, Mastercard is responsible for information security and must: Abide by Mastercard’s security policies and practices; Ensure the confidentiality and integrity of the information being accessed; Report any suspected information security violation or breach, and Complete all periodic mandatory security trainings in accordance with Mastercard’s guidelines.

jobs.jd:
Who we are 

At Twilio, we’re shaping the future of communications, all from the comfort of our homes. We deliver innovative solutions to hundreds of thousands of businesses and empower millions of developers worldwide to craft personalized customer experiences.

Our dedication to remote-first work, and strong culture of connection and global inclusion means that no matter your location, you’re part of a vibrant team with diverse experiences making a global impact each day. As we continue to revolutionize how the world interacts, we’re acquiring new skills and experiences that make work feel truly rewarding. Your career at Twilio is in your hands.
.

Hiring and how we work

We use Artificial Intelligence (AI) to help make our hiring process efficient. That said, every hiring decision is made by real Twilions! 

Also, while we are a remote-first company, you may be asked to report in person on an ad-hoc basis for team gatherings, functional off-sites or customer meetings. 
.

See yourself at Twilio

Join the team as Twilio’s next Machine Learning Engineer, Customer Memory.

About the job

This position is needed to build and scale the pipelines that turn raw conversation data into structured, searchable customer memory, and the evaluation systems that keep that memory accurate as the product evolves.

You'll join the Conversation Memory team, which builds the memory layer behind Twilio's Conversational AI platform: the systems that extract what matters from millions of conversations, resolve it to the right customer, and retrieve it in milliseconds when an agent needs it. Memory that is wrong, stale, or crossed between customers is worse than no memory at all, so quality measurement is a first-class part of the work.

Responsibilities

In this role, you’ll:

  • Build the extraction pipeline that turns raw data into structured memory, tuning the LLM prompts and schemas that decide what an AI agent remembers about a customer and what it forgets.
  • Own the retrieval path that answers "what do we know about this person?" in milliseconds, working with embeddings, vector search, and ranking
  • Contribute to the eval systems that tell us whether memory is actually getting better, turning a fuzzy question of quality into benchmarks and regression gates that run before every change ships.
  • Diagnose production issues across the ingestion, extraction, and indexing path using logs, metrics, and traces.
  • Partner with Product and ML teams to translate customer problems into system changes and evaluation criteria.

Qualifications 

Twilio values diverse experiences from all kinds of industries, and we encourage everyone who meets the required qualifications to apply. If your career is just starting or hasn't followed a traditional path, don't let that stop you from considering Twilio. We are always looking for people who will bring something new to the table!

Required:

  • Experience building backend services, and a demonstrated ability to pick up new languages, frameworks, and tools as the problem demands.
  • A curious approach to service management: ability to investigate how systems actually behave in production, and desire to continuously learn how to operate them with rigor and accountability.
  • Experience building or working with evaluation/quality-measurement systems, such as regression detection or quality metrics, or the desire to learn.
  • Solid grounding in observability practices: structured logging, metrics, and using them to debug distributed systems in production.
  • Fluency with AI-assisted dev tools (e.g. agents for code generation, review, debugging), applied with deliberate direction and critical thinking.

Desired:

  • Experience with Go and/or Python.
  • Experience with event-streaming systems (e.g. Kafka).
  • Experience building LLM-backed products.
  • Practical experience applying ML, e.g. building, evaluating, or productionizing models.

Location

  • This role will be remote, but is not eligible to be hired in San Francisco, CA, Oakland, CA, San Jose, CA, or the surrounding areas.

Travel

We prioritize connection and opportunities to build relationships with our customers and each other. For this role, you may be required to travel occasionally to participate in project or team in-person meetings.

What We Offer

Working at Twilio offers many benefits, including competitive pay, generous time off, ample parental and wellness leave, healthcare, a retirement savings program, and much more. Offerings vary by location.

When you see the same opportunity across customers, your work can change where OpenAI invests. Trace customer activity across channels to distinguish new use cases from traffic that moved from the direct API. - Identify where customers are ready to scale. Combine what account teams hear with evidence on request failures, latency, and model availability. Work with Product and Engineering on a change and measure what happens to usage. - Shape growth plans with GTM and Finance. Estimate what existing workloads and upcoming launches can contribute by year end, test the assumptions that matter most, and recommend where to focus with each provider. - Own the consumption forecast. Qualifications - Experience independently leading data science work on a product, growth, or commercial question that changed a business decision. - Strong SQL and Python skills. Key Responsibilities Serve as the business analytics domain expert for Workday Data Cloud, providing technical and strategic thought leadership. jobs.title: Senior Machine Learning Engineer (W/M/X)
jobs.jd: Ubisoft is natively data-driven: from the core of our games to our marketing actions, we’re leveraging data and algorithms. Part of the Ubisoft Data Office, our team operates within the Player Domain, focusing on player safety and security. We build and deploy machine learning systems that keep our players protected — from detecting sanction circumvention using Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) to real-time identification of toxic chat using transformer models. Our scope is broad: NLP, anomaly detection, graph learning, and large language models. Your role: Build scalable machine learning systems to preserve the trust and safety of our players. Our motto is to never stop at the prototyping phase — we combine research and engineering cycles with the objective of deploying production-grade products that have a real impact at scale. You will tackle hard problems at the intersection of NLP, anomaly detection, graph learning, and LLMs. We are looking for a Senior Machine Learning Engineer with proven production experience, someone comfortable moving fluidly between research and engineering. Missions: The archetypal missions for this position would be to: Design, train, and deploy ML models across a range of player safety and security use cases, spanning NLP, anomaly detection, and graph-based learning. Evaluate and implement state-of-the-art ML techniques — adapting the latest research in deep learning, NLP, and graph learning to production constraints, implementing from scratch when needed. Take full ownership of the projects you build: interact with stakeholders, define success metrics, monitor live systems, and iterate. Write, optimise, and ship high-quality code that runs at scale, applying modern MLOps best practices (CI/CD, model versioning, observability). In collaboration with data and software engineers, deliver models and prediction pipelines to production on our internal or public cloud infrastructures. Strong Python software engineering skills: clean code, testing, documentation, CI/CD. Proven experience deploying and monitoring production ML models (MLOps, model serving, drift monitoring). Hands-on experience with NLP / LLMs: fine-tuning transformer models, prompt engineering, RAG, or LLM-based pipelines. Experience with graph-based ML (GNNs) is a strong plus. Knowledge of anomaly detection or fraud/trust & safety systems in a production context. Experience with distributed data processing (Spark) and cloud data platforms; familiarity with Databricks (DAB, Delta Live Tables) or Azure-specific services is a plus. Strong communication skills; English is mandatory (presentations, cross-team collaboration, reporting). Ideal candidate: experience with token classification (NER, sequence labelling) and/or hands-on GNN training (node classification, link prediction, graph construction pipelines). Ubisoft's perks 💰 Profit Sharing, yearly company saving plan. 25 paid time off + 12 additional paid days off. 50% of your transportation pass is paid by the company, lunch vouchers (9€/day), healthcare for you and your family, and lots of Ubisoft additional perks. 👶 Maternity leaves of 20 weeks, paternity/co-parental leaves of 7 weeks. 📍 Our office is located in Saint Mandé, (Metro line 1, Saint Mandé station). Gym available in the building. Information about Ubisoft Ubisoft offers the same job opportunities to all, without any distinction of gender, ethnicity, religion, sexual orientation, social status, disability, or age. Ubisoft ensures the development of an inclusive work environment which mirrors the diversity of our gamers’ community.

jobs.title: Machine Learning Engineer – Practice IA MARGO
jobs.jd: Qui sommes nous ? Chez MARGO, nos consultants travaillent sur ce qui compte vraiment : des projets complexes qui allient challenge intellectuel et impact business réel. C’est pourquoi nous accompagnons les plus grands acteurs de la finance, de l’industrie et de la tech sur leurs projets les plus stratégiques en Data Science, Machine Learning et Intelligence Artificielle. Pourquoi rejoindre la practice IA ? Vous évoluerez au sein d’une équipe encadrée par Hamza Bouanani, Practice Manager IA chez MARGO, également Lead Data Scientist chez BNP Paribas. Travailler à ses côtés, c’est intégrer une équipe d’experts passionnés, être challengé sur le plan technique et méthodologique, et contribuer à des projets à fort impact pour les clients. Vos missions Nous recherchons un Machine Learning Engineer pour rejoindre nos équipes et intervenir au cœur de la stratégie Data de nos clients (Industrie, Finance, Énergie). Votre objectif principal sera d'industrialiser les algorithmes de Machine Learning et de garantir leur cycle de vie en production. Vous interviendrez sur trois axes techniques majeurs : 1. Industrialisation & Déploiement (Model Serving) - Transformation des modèles de recherche (Proof of Concept) en code de production robuste, testé et optimisé. - Développement d'APIs performantes (FastAPI, Flask) pour exposer les modèles aux applications métiers. - Conteneurisation des solutions (Docker) et orchestration sur des clusters (Kubernetes) pour assurer la scalabilité et la haute disponibilité. 2. Architecture MLOps & Automatisation - Conception et maintenance de pipelines CI/CD dédiés au Machine Learning (réentraînement automatique, validation des modèles). - Mise en place et gestion d'outils d'orchestration de flux de données (Airflow, Kubeflow, Dagster). - Gestion du versioning des données et des modèles (DVC, MLflow) pour assurer la reproductibilité des expériences. 3. Performance & Optimisation - Optimisation des temps de réponse (latence) et de l'utilisation des ressources de calcul (CPU/GPU). - Refactoring de code pour respecter les standards de Software Craftsmanship (Clean Code, TDD). - Gestion des Feature Stores pour centraliser et servir les variables calculées en temps réel. Votre rôle inclura également : Monitoring avancé : Mise en place de sondes pour détecter le "Data Drift" (dérive des données) ou le "Model Drift" et déclencher des alertes proactives. Collaboration transverse : Faire le pont entre les Data Scientists (mathématiques/modélisation) et les Data Engineers (infrastructure/données) pour fluidifier les mises en production. Évangélisation : Diffuser les bonnes pratiques de développement logiciel au sein des équipes Data Science. Profil recherché Nous cherchons un profil hybride, à la frontière entre le Software Engineering et la Data Science, capable de comprendre les mathématiques sous-jacentes tout en maîtrisant les contraintes de production informatique. - Formation : Bac+5 (école d’ingénieur, université) en Informatique ou Mathématiques Appliquées. - Compétences Techniques Cœurs : * Maîtrise avancée de Python et des bonnes pratiques logicielles (Git, Tests unitaires/d'intégration, Packaging). * Solide expérience sur les plateformes Cloud (AWS, Azure ou GCP) et l'IaC (Terraform est un plus). * Maîtrise de l'écosystème MLOps : MLflow, Kubeflow, Docker, Kubernetes. - Connaissances Data : Bonne compréhension des bibliothèques ML (Scikit-learn, Pandas) et Deep Learning (TensorFlow, PyTorch) pour pouvoir optimiser le code des Data Scientists. - Expérience : Vous avez une expérience significative dans le déploiement de modèles ML en production (batch ou temps réel). - Mindset : * Rigueur absolue sur la qualité du code et l'automatisation. * Goût pour la résolution de problèmes d'architecture complexes. * Capacité à travailler dans des environnements techniques hétérogènes. Ce que nous offrons - Des missions ambitieuses et variées, toujours sélectionnées pour leur valeur ajoutée ; - Un accompagnement de proximité par des experts reconnus ; - Une communauté d’ingénieurs passionnés, avec workshops, conférences et échanges réguliers ; - Une culture d’exigence technique, de partage des connaissances et de développement continu. La suite ? Premier entretien : Échangez avec un recruteur et un business developer Entretien Technique : Montrez vos compétences et recevez un retour d'expérience Entretien de Motivation : Rencontrez un membre du comité de direction ENGAGEMENT POUR L'INCLUSION MARGO s'engage à offrir des opportunités égales à tous, nous cultivons un environnement de travail inclusif qui valorise la diversité. jobs.title: Lead Data Scientist (Graph Analytics)

fraud, merchant, cybersecurity, and threat-intelligence data. • Provide technical leadership for graph analytics and modeling, including graph schema design, relationship modeling, community detection, link analysis, graph embeddings, and graph neural networks – all in service of addressing real-world cybersecurity problems such as breaches, payment card testing, and scam rings. • Develop models and analytical methods that identify complex or indirect risk patterns across interconnected entities such as payment cards, merchants, domains, service providers, fraud events, digital skimmers, technologies, vulnerabilities, and threat-intelligence indicators • Apply graph algorithms and machine learning techniques to identify hidden communities, shared infrastructure, anomalous relationships, compromise paths, and patterns that cannot be sufficiently captured through transaction-level or entity-level models alone. • Work hands-on with Python, SQL, Spark, Hadoop, and monitoring requirements, and business-outcome measures for machine learning solutions. • Translate ambiguous business, product, cybersecurity, and fraud problems into clearly defined analytical approaches, technical requirements, and delivery plans. • Partner closely with product, data engineering, software engineering, cybersecurity, operations, and other data science teams to move analytical capabilities from research through production deployment. • Communicate analytical findings, model performance, technical tradeoffs, risks, and business implications clearly to technical jobs.title: Data Scientist III (AmSec), Veritas

jobs.jd:

Whether it’s building award-winning games or crafting engine technology that enables others to make visually stunning interactive experiences, we’re always innovating.

Being Epic means being a part of a team that continually strives to do right by our community and users. We’re constantly innovating to raise the bar of engine and game development.

ENGINEERING - GAMES

What We Do

Unreal projects have been leading the pack of real-time entertainment with our constantly growing team of engineering experts. We’re always improving on the tools and technology that empower content developers worldwide.

What You'll Do

You will work with our team of applied research engineers at the intersection of computer vision,  gameplay agents, natural language processing, and machine learning to create state-of-the-art tools to support game developers in our ecosystem with a focus on bots (trained gameplay agents, intelligent NPCs, companions, world modeling), as well as automation of a number key areas (including moderation, security, and QA testing). You will be responsible for the design, implementation and deployment of production-ready machine learning models that can be integrated in our ecosystem.

In this role, you will

  • Create and deliver production-ready, scalable and high-quality machine learning models and associated algorithms that can make actions in game environments
  • Critically assess the effectiveness of such models and make recommendations for the ongoing roadmap
  • Methodically understand and assess the effectiveness of new data channels and support collection/creation of new ones

What we're looking for

    • PhD in Computer Science, Mathematics or related field, or 3+ years of relevant industry experience 
    • Experience creating / applying machine learning algorithms for action modeling of bots behavior, vision-based or language-instructed, and deploying them as production-level systems in-game
    • Expert, hands-on knowledge of:
      • Deep learning, incl. but not limited to applications in the gaming industry
      • Foundational models and vision and/or language, especially  vision-language-action models, reinforcement learning agents, incl. local deployment and model post-training of open weights models
      • Reinforcement learning, incl. experience with agentic systems, reward design, policy optimisation, evaluation, and building scalable training environments for agents
      • Python and associated ML tools/frameworks (numpy, scipy, sklearn, pytorch)
    • Experience with working collaboratively with other developers, following a flexible/agile/lean approach

EPIC JOB + EPIC BENEFITS = EPIC LIFE

We pay 100% for benefits except for PMI (for dependents). jobs.title: Software Engineer II - AI/ML, Neuron Inference, Neuron Inference
